components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.
贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money and value, as in 财, 买; 质 is the real value or substance of something.

example.hanzi: 了解事物的本质比记住表面现象更重要。
example.pinyin: liǎojiě shìwù de běnzhì bǐ jìzhù biǎomiàn xiànxiàng gèng zhòngyào.
example.english: Understanding the essential nature of things matters more than memorizing surface appearances.
example.fact: Dmitri Mendeleev's 1869 periodic table organized elements by their essential, underlying properties rather than superficial traits, and it was accurate enough that he could confidently predict the existence of several elements that had not yet been discovered.

examples.hanzi: 这两件事的本质是一样的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiàn shì de běnzhì shì yīyàng de.
examples.english: The essence of these two things is the same.

examples.hanzi: 他的本质并不坏，只是有点固执。
examples.pinyin: Tā de běnzhì bìng bù huài, zhǐshì yǒudiǎn gùzhí.
examples.english: He is not bad by nature, just a bit stubborn.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person leaning to one side; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
扁 (biǎn) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 篇 piān and 遍 biàn.
见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.

example.hanzi: 我们应该努力克服对他人的偏见。
example.pinyin: wǒmen yīnggāi nǔlì kèfú duì tārén de piānjiàn.
example.english: We should work hard to overcome our prejudices against others.
example.fact: In the 1954 Robbers Cave experiment, psychologist Muzafer Sherif split boys at a summer camp into two groups and found that simply competing over shared resources was enough to spark strong prejudice between them within days — a rift that was reduced only once the groups were later given a shared goal to work toward together.

examples.hanzi: 不要对不同地方的人有偏见。
examples.pinyin: Bù yào duì bùtóng dìfang de rén yǒu piānjiàn.
examples.english: Don't be prejudiced against people from different places.

examples.hanzi: 他用事实打破了大家的偏见。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng shìshí dǎpò le dàjiā de piānjiàn.
examples.english: He broke everyone's bias with facts.

components.note: 唐 (táng) — the Tang dynasty; as a part it sounds out 糖 táng and 塘 táng.

example.hanzi: 唐朝的诗歌很有名。
example.pinyin: Tángcháo de shīgē hěn yǒumíng.
example.english: Tang dynasty poetry is very famous.
example.fact: 唐 (618-907) is seen as a golden age: 唐诗 (Tang poetry), 唐三彩 (Tang tricolour pottery). Overseas, 唐人街 (Chinatown) means 'Tang people's street', and 唐 is a surname.

examples.hanzi: 我在唐人街吃了一顿饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài Tángrénjiē chī le yí dùn fàn.
examples.english: I had a meal in Chinatown.

examples.hanzi: 他是我的同事，姓唐。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de tóngshì, xìng Táng.
examples.english: He is my colleague and his surname is Tang.

components.note: 土 (earth) — levelling the ground, hence even; also in 地 ground, 城 city.
匀 (yún) gives a close sound and the idea of even; it also sounds out 钧 jūn.

example.hanzi: 这批货的质量均合格。
example.pinyin: Zhè pī huò de zhìliàng jūn hégé.
example.english: The quality of this batch of goods is all up to standard.
example.fact: 均 as an adverb means 'all, without exception' and is formal: 均可 (all are acceptable). It is the core of 平均 (average) and 均匀 (even, uniform).

examples.hanzi: 大家的成绩均在八十分以上。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā de chéngjì jūn zài bāshí fēn yǐshàng.
examples.english: Everyone's grades are above eighty.

examples.hanzi: 每个人平均每天走一万步。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge rén píngjūn měitiān zǒu yíwàn bù.
examples.english: On average each person walks ten thousand steps a day.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money and value, as in 财, 买; 质 is the real value or substance of something.

example.hanzi: 这家店的东西质量很好。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de dōngxi zhìliàng hěn hǎo.
example.english: The goods in this shop are of good quality.
example.fact: 质 is a bound form seen in 质量 (quality; also 'mass' in physics), 品质 (character), 物质 (matter), 本质 (essence) and 质问 (to question sharply).

examples.hanzi: 这个牌子的质量很可靠。
examples.pinyin: Zhège páizi de zhìliàng hěn kěkào.
examples.english: The quality of this brand is very reliable.

examples.hanzi: 这里的水质很好，可以直接喝。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de shuǐzhì hěn hǎo, kěyǐ zhíjiē hē.
examples.english: The water quality here is good and you can drink it directly.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 浮 is floating on water.
孚 (fú) — same sound: 浮 fú. 孚 also sounds out 俘 fú and 孵 fū.

example.hanzi: 木头能浮在水上。
example.pinyin: Mùtou néng fú zài shuǐ shang.
example.english: Wood can float on water.
example.fact: 浮 means floating (浮在水上) and, figuratively, shallow or restless: 浮躁 (impatient), 浮华 (flashy), 浮云 (fleeting clouds, an image of worldly things).

examples.hanzi: 游泳时，他仰面浮在水上。
examples.pinyin: Yóuyǒng shí, tā yǎngmiàn fú zài shuǐ shàng.
examples.english: When swimming, he floats on his back on the water.

examples.hanzi: 天上浮着几朵白云。
examples.pinyin: Tiān shàng fú zhe jǐ duǒ báiyún.
examples.english: A few white clouds float in the sky.

components.note: 角 (horn) — an ox's horn; with 刀 (knife) the picture is cutting up an ox, so "to take apart", then to loosen and explain.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 分, 切, 到; a blade separates the parts.
攵 (tap, strike) — marks actions, as in 教, 改, 放; 散 is to scatter (sàn) or to be loose (sǎn).

example.hanzi: 会议结束后，大家陆续解散离开了。
example.pinyin: huìyì jiéshù hòu, dàjiā lùxù jiěsàn líkāile.
example.english: After the meeting ended, everyone gradually dispersed and left.
example.fact: The League of Nations, founded after World War I to prevent future conflicts, formally dissolved in April 1946 after failing to stop World War II, transferring its assets and mission to the newly created United Nations.

examples.hanzi: 公司因为亏损而解散了。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī yīnwèi kuīsǔn ér jiěsàn le.
examples.english: The company disbanded because of losses.

examples.hanzi: 教练说完话，球员们就解散了。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoliàn shuō wán huà, qiúyuánmen jiù jiěsàn le.
examples.english: After the coach finished speaking, the players dispersed.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 土 is earth and ground, as in 地, 城, 块; 坦 is level ground, then open and frank.
旦 (dàn) — near sound — 坦 is tǎn; 旦 also sounds out 但 dàn and 担 dān.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 请; 诚 is honest speech.
成 (chéng) — same sound — 诚 is chéng, like 成; 成 also sounds out 城 chéng.

example.hanzi: 他坦诚地承认了自己的错误。
example.pinyin: tā tǎnchéng de chéngrèn le zìjǐ de cuòwù.
example.english: He candidly admitted his own mistake.
example.fact: When English painter Peter Lely was commissioned to paint Oliver Cromwell in the 1650s, Cromwell reportedly insisted the portrait show him "warts and all," rejecting the flattering idealization typical of royal and noble portraiture at the time.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要坦诚地交换意见。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào tǎnchéng de jiāohuàn yìjiàn.
examples.english: We need to exchange opinions frankly.

examples.hanzi: 朋友之间应该坦诚相待。
examples.pinyin: Péngyou zhījiān yīnggāi tǎnchéng xiāngdài.
examples.english: Friends should treat each other with honesty.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.
罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and entrapment: 罗 net, 罚 punish, 骂 scold; here a net of wrongdoing 非 catching the guilty.
非 (not, wrong) — what is wrong or unlawful; in 罪 it is the wrongdoing caught in the net.

example.hanzi: 没有确凿的证据，法院无法对他定罪。
example.pinyin: méiyǒu quèzáo de zhèngjù, fǎyuàn wúfǎ duì tā dìngzuì.
example.english: Without solid evidence, the court could not convict him.
example.fact: Colin Pitchfork became the first person in the world convicted of murder using DNA fingerprinting evidence, in a landmark 1988 UK case that also cleared an innocent suspect who had earlier confessed under police pressure.

examples.hanzi: 法院根据证据对他定罪。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn gēnjù zhèngjù duì tā dìngzuì.
examples.english: The court convicted him based on the evidence.

examples.hanzi: 他被定罪后，被判了五年。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi dìngzuì hòu, bèi pàn le wǔ nián.
examples.english: After being convicted, he was sentenced to five years.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) with 月 — the shady side of a hill, the opposite of 阳 (阝 with 日, sunny); yīn is the dark principle.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 这 this, 过 pass, 近 near; a 道 is a road, then a way or principle.
首 (shǒu, head) is only a loose sound hint for dào; 首 also means "head/first", fitting a lead-the-way road.

example.hanzi: 妇科医生建议她每年做一次阴道检查。
example.pinyin: fùkē yīshēng jiànyì tā měinián zuò yī cì yīndào jiǎnchá.
example.english: The gynecologist recommended she have a vaginal exam once a year.
example.fact: Platypuses and echidnas, known as monotremes, are the only mammals that lay eggs instead of giving live birth, representing an ancient evolutionary branch that split off before most other mammalian traits, including live birth, had evolved.

examples.hanzi: 这种感染会引起阴道不适，需要及时治疗。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng gǎnrǎn huì yǐnqǐ yīndào bùshì, xūyào jíshí zhìliáo.
examples.english: This infection causes vaginal discomfort and needs prompt treatment.

examples.hanzi: 医学课上，老师讲解了阴道的结构。
examples.pinyin: Yīxué kè shàng, lǎoshī jiǎngjiě le yīndào de jiégòu.
examples.english: In medical class, the teacher explained the structure of the vagina.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 海上贸易促进了古代不同文明之间的交流。
example.pinyin: Hǎishàng màoyì cùjìnle gǔdài bùtóng wénmíng zhī jiān de jiāoliú.
example.english: Maritime trade promoted exchange between different ancient civilizations.
example.fact: The Maritime Silk Road connected China to East Africa and the Persian Gulf as early as the 2nd century BC, carrying not just silk but ceramics, spices, and ideas across monsoon-driven sea lanes. Zheng He's fifteenth-century treasure fleets, some ships over 100 meters long, sailed these same routes decades before European age-of-exploration voyages. The winds that powered these journeys, the Indian Ocean monsoons, reverse direction seasonally, letting sailors ride one wind out and the opposite wind home.

examples.hanzi: 海上的风浪很大，渔船都回港了。
examples.pinyin: Hǎishàng de fēnglàng hěn dà, yúchuán dōu huí gǎng le.
examples.english: The waves at sea are huge, so the fishing boats all returned to port.

examples.hanzi: 我们在海上漂了三天才看到陆地。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài hǎishàng piāo le sān tiān cái kàndào lùdì.
examples.english: We drifted on the sea for three days before we saw land.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
艹 stands in for 竹 (bamboo) in the traditional 節, bamboo joints: sections, then festivals and knots.

example.hanzi: 每年二月十四号是情人节。
example.pinyin: Měi nián èr yuè shísì hào shì Qíngrénjié.
example.english: Every year, February 14th is Valentine's Day.
example.fact: Valentine's Day traces back to a Roman festival called Lupercalia, a mid-February fertility rite involving animal sacrifice and matchmaking lotteries, later Christianized and attached to Saint Valentine. Feb 14 became linked with romance in medieval Europe partly through Geoffrey Chaucer's poem "Parliament of Fowls," which imagined birds choosing mates on that day. Today the holiday drives one of the largest annual spikes in global flower exports, with millions of roses flown from Colombia and Ecuador to North America and Europe in the week beforehand.

examples.hanzi: 情人节那天，他送了她一束玫瑰花。
examples.pinyin: Qíngrénjié nà tiān, tā sòng le tā yī shù méiguihuā.
examples.english: On Valentine's Day, he gave her a bouquet of roses.

examples.hanzi: 情人节的餐厅很难订位，要提前预约。
examples.pinyin: Qíngrénjié de cāntīng hěn nán dìng wèi, yào tíqián yùyuē.
examples.english: Restaurants are hard to book on Valentine's Day, so reserve ahead.

components.note: 来 (come, wheat) — traditional 麥 combined 來 (the old word for the wheat plant) with a foot 夂 — a grain brought in; 麦 is the wheat radical.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.
風 (traditional wind) — 风 is the simplified form of 風, which had 凡 (fán) as a loose sound hint around 虫; the simplified shape is just a reduced form.

example.hanzi: 歌手拿起麦克风开始唱歌。
example.pinyin: Gēshǒu ná qǐ màikèfēng kāishǐ chànggē.
example.english: The singer picked up the microphone and started singing.
example.fact: The first practical microphone, built by Emile Berliner in 1877, used carbon granules whose electrical resistance changed as sound waves compressed them, the same carbon-button design that powered telephone handsets for a century. Modern condenser microphones instead measure tiny shifts in capacitance as sound moves a thin charged diaphragm, letting them capture frequencies far beyond human hearing for scientific recording. NASA has flown specialized microphones on Mars rovers, and Perseverance's 2021 recordings were the first audio ever captured on another planet's surface.

examples.hanzi: 麦克风没有声音，你检查一下。
examples.pinyin: Màikèfēng méiyǒu shēngyīn, nǐ jiǎnchá yīxià.
examples.english: The microphone has no sound, so please check it.

examples.hanzi: 开会时请把麦克风调到静音。
examples.pinyin: Kāihuì shí qǐng bǎ màikèfēng tiáo dào jìngyīn.
examples.english: Please mute your microphone during the meeting.

components.note: 身 (body) — the body ducking away; also in 躺 lie down, 躬.
朵 (duǒ) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 垛 duò.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 他及时躲开了迎面而来的自行车。
example.pinyin: Tā jíshí duǒkāile yíngmiàn ér lái de zìxíngchē.
example.english: He dodged the oncoming bicycle just in time.
example.fact: The reflex that lets a person dodge a sudden obstacle, the startle response, travels through the brainstem rather than the slower conscious cortex, which is why a flinch happens roughly 100 milliseconds before a person is even aware of the threat. Fighter pilots train specifically to override this reflex when it works against high-speed maneuvering. Octopuses show an even faster version: touch receptors on their skin can trigger evasive jetting without any signal reaching the central brain at all.

examples.hanzi: 看到狗跑过来，他赶紧躲开了。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào gǒu pǎo guòlái, tā gǎnjǐn duǒkāi le.
examples.english: Seeing the dog running over, he quickly dodged out of the way.

examples.hanzi: 她一直在躲开那个讨厌的邻居。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīzhí zài duǒkāi nàge tǎoyàn de línjū.
examples.english: She has been avoiding that annoying neighbor.

components.note: 弟 (dì) is a sound clue for 第 dì, 梯 tī and 剃 tì; as a word it means younger brother.
儿 (person, legs) — with 口 mouth on top: the elder brother who speaks for the family. 兄 also in 况 kuàng.

example.hanzi: 他们从小一起长大，感情就像亲弟兄一样。
example.pinyin: Tāmen cóngxiǎo yìqǐ zhǎngdà, gǎnqíng jiù xiàng qīn dìxiong yíyàng.
example.english: They grew up together and feel like real brothers.
example.fact: Behavioral studies of wolf packs show that non-breeding 'brother' wolves often help raise their siblings' pups, a pattern called cooperative breeding that increases the survival odds of shared genes even without direct parenthood. The same strategy appears in naked mole rats and many bird species, where older siblings delay their own reproduction to support the family group. Evolutionary biologists explain this sibling cooperation partly through kin selection, the idea that helping a close relative reproduce can be nearly as effective, genetically, as reproducing oneself.

examples.hanzi: 弟兄们，我们一起加油干！
examples.pinyin: Dìxiongmen, wǒmen yīqǐ jiāyóu gàn!
examples.english: Brothers, let's work hard together!

examples.hanzi: 他有三个弟兄，都住在老家。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu sān gè dìxiong, dōu zhù zài lǎojiā.
examples.english: He has three brothers, all living in his hometown.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — a bird over a flame is scorched. 焦 also sounds out 蕉 jiāo and 礁 jiāo.
灬 (fire, 四点底) — flames at the bottom, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 煮 cook.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 这个问题成了会议讨论的焦点。
example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí chéngle huìyì tǎolùn de jiāodiǎn.
example.english: This issue became the focal point of the meeting's discussion.
example.fact: In optics, a lens's focal point is where parallel light rays converge after refraction, and the distance to that point, the focal length, determines how strongly a lens bends light. The same principle scaled up let Archimedes, according to legend, use curved mirrors to focus sunlight and ignite enemy ships at the siege of Syracuse in 214 BC. Modern solar power towers use an array of thousands of mirrors to focus sunlight onto a single receiver, reaching temperatures above 1,000 degrees Celsius.

examples.hanzi: 这位明星成了媒体关注的焦点。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi míngxīng chéng le méitǐ guānzhù de jiāodiǎn.
examples.english: This star became the focus of media attention.

examples.hanzi: 相机的焦点没对准，照片是模糊的。
examples.pinyin: Xiàngjī de jiāodiǎn méi duìzhǔn, zhàopiàn shì móhu de.
examples.english: The camera wasn't focused properly, so the photo is blurry.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
耳 (ear) — ear radical, as in 聪 clever, 聋 deaf, 闻 to hear.
止 (zhǐ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 址 zhǐ and 趾 zhǐ.

example.hanzi: 他做出这种事，真是无耻。
example.pinyin: Tā zuòchū zhè zhǒng shì, zhēn shì wúchǐ.
example.english: What he did is truly shameless.
example.fact: Charles Darwin argued that the physical sign of shame, blushing, is the most human and least controllable of all expressions, since almost no one can blush at will. Psychologists distinguish shame, a painful sense of one's whole self being flawed, from guilt, which focuses on a specific bad act; cultures vary widely in which emotion carries more social weight. Researchers studying psychopathy have found that a diminished capacity for shame is one of its most consistent and measurable traits.

examples.hanzi: 骗老人的钱真是太无耻了。
examples.pinyin: Piàn lǎorén de qián zhēn shì tài wúchǐ le.
examples.english: Cheating old people out of money is truly shameless.

examples.hanzi: 他无耻地撒了谎，还不肯道歉。
examples.pinyin: Tā wúchǐ de sā le huǎng, hái bù kěn dàoqiàn.
examples.english: He shamelessly lied and still refuses to apologize.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打 hit, 拿 take, 把 hold; 抱 is to hug or hold in the arms.
包 (bāo) is a close sound clue for bào; it also sounds out 跑 pǎo, 饱 bǎo and 炮 pào.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打 hit, 拿 take, 把 hold; 抱 is to hug or hold in the arms.
包 (bāo) is a close sound clue for bào; it also sounds out 跑 pǎo, 饱 bǎo and 炮 pào.

example.hanzi: 小孩摔倒了，妈妈赶紧抱抱他。
example.pinyin: Xiǎohái shuāidǎole, māma gǎnjǐn bàobao tā.
example.english: The child fell down, and mom quickly gave him a hug.
example.fact: A hug lasting roughly 20 seconds triggers a measurable release of oxytocin, a hormone that lowers cortisol and blood pressure, according to studies from the University of North Carolina. Touch researchers have also found that even hugging a pet or a weighted blanket can produce a milder version of this calming effect, since the pressure receptors involved don't distinguish much between sources. Some primates, notably bonobos, use embracing and other physical contact specifically to defuse group tension after conflicts, a behavior researchers call reconciliation.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝想让妈妈抱抱。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao xiǎng ràng māma bàobao.
examples.english: The baby wants Mom to hold her.

examples.hanzi: 来，让我抱抱你，别难过了。
examples.pinyin: Lái, ràng wǒ bàobao nǐ, bié nánguò le.
examples.english: Come here, let me give you a hug, don't be sad.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; here the word for still or again.
乃 (nǎi) is a loose sound hint; 扔 rēng shares the same part.
旧 (simplified 舊) — old; the old sound part 臼 (jiù) also gives 舅 jiù (uncle).

example.hanzi: 虽然搬了新家，他仍旧每天去那家老咖啡店。
example.pinyin: Suīrán bānle xīn jiā, tā réngjiù měitiān qù nà jiā lǎo kāfēidiàn.
example.english: Even though he moved to a new home, he still goes to that old coffee shop every day.
example.fact: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, carved into a mountainside in the Arctic, preserves millions of crop seeds at minus 18 degrees Celsius, designed to remain viable for centuries even if outside power fails, since the surrounding permafrost keeps the chamber cold on its own. During the Syrian civil war, researchers withdrew seeds from Svalbard to restart a damaged gene bank in Aleppo, the vault's first real-world use. Some seeds inside, like certain wheat varieties, are estimated to remain plantable after more than a thousand years in ideal frozen storage.

examples.hanzi: 十年过去了，她仍旧住在那条小巷里。
examples.pinyin: Shí nián guòqù le, tā réngjiù zhù zài nà tiáo xiǎoxiàng lǐ.
examples.english: Ten years have passed, and she still lives in that little alley.

examples.hanzi: 虽然下了雨，比赛仍旧照常进行。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán xià le yǔ, bǐsài réngjiù zhàocháng jìnxíng.
examples.english: Although it rained, the game still went on as usual.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — crops and seasons, as in 种 plant, 秋 autumn, 稻 rice.
子 (child) — 季 was the youngest child, then the last month of a season, then the season itself.
艹 stands in for 竹 (bamboo) in the traditional 節, bamboo joints: sections, then festivals and knots.

example.hanzi: 这里四个季节的变化非常明显。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ sì gè jìjié de biànhuà fēicháng míngxiǎn.
example.english: The change of the four seasons here is very noticeable.
example.fact: Earth's seasons are caused not by distance from the sun but by its 23.4-degree axial tilt, which shifts which hemisphere receives more direct sunlight over the year; Earth is actually closest to the sun in January, during the Northern Hemisphere's winter. Some regions near the equator experience only two real seasons, wet and dry, driven by shifting monsoon winds rather than temperature swings. On Uranus, whose axis tilts a full 98 degrees, each pole faces 21 years of continuous sunlight followed by 21 years of darkness in a single 'season.'

examples.hanzi: 你最喜欢哪个季节？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuì xǐhuan nǎge jìjié?
examples.english: Which season do you like best?

examples.hanzi: 现在是吃西瓜的好季节。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài shì chī xīguā de hǎo jìjié.
examples.english: Now is a good season for eating watermelon.

components.note: 戈 (halberd, weapon) — war and weapons: 我, 成, 武, 伐; here fighting.
占 (zhàn) sounds exactly like 战; also in 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
各 (gè) is only a loose hint for lüè; 路 lù and 络 luò share it.

example.hanzi: 公司调整了未来五年的发展战略。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī tiáozhěngle wèilái wǔ nián de fāzhǎn zhànlüè.
example.english: The company adjusted its development strategy for the next five years.
example.fact: The oldest known written treatise on strategy, Sun Tzu's "The Art of War," was composed around the 5th century BC and still appears on modern military academy reading lists alongside works from Clausewitz two millennia later. Game theory, developed largely by John von Neumann in the 20th century, gave strategy a mathematical footing by modeling how rational actors choose among competing options, work that later underpinned Cold War nuclear deterrence policy. Chess engines like AlphaZero eventually surpassed human strategic play not by memorizing openings but by learning strategy from scratch through millions of self-played games.

examples.hanzi: 这是公司长远发展的重要战略。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì gōngsī chángyuǎn fāzhǎn de zhòngyào zhànlüè.
examples.english: This is an important strategy for the company's long-term growth.

examples.hanzi: 他们制定了新的市场战略。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhìdìng le xīn de shìchǎng zhànlüè.
examples.english: They formulated a new market strategy.

components.note: 水 (water) — a picture of flowing water; as a radical it appears as 氵 on the left (海, 河) or 水 at the bottom (泉, 冰).
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.hanzi: 冬天太冷，水管冻裂了。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān tài lěng, shuǐguǎn dòng lièle.
example.english: It was too cold in winter, and the water pipe froze and burst.
example.fact: Ancient Rome's aqueduct and pipe network supplied the city with an estimated one billion liters of water a day at its peak, more per capita than many modern cities, using lead pipes called 'fistulae' whose manufacturer stamps still survive. Roman engineers understood gravity-fed flow well enough to build aqueducts with gradients as gentle as 1 in 4,800 over dozens of kilometers. Pipes freezing and bursting today happens because water expands roughly 9% in volume when it turns to ice, generating enough internal pressure to split even sturdy metal.

examples.hanzi: 厨房的水管漏水了，请人来修一下。
examples.pinyin: Chúfáng de shuǐguǎn lòushuǐ le, qǐng rén lái xiū yīxià.
examples.english: The kitchen water pipe is leaking, so get someone to fix it.

examples.hanzi: 工人正在更换老房子的水管。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrén zhèngzài gēnghuàn lǎo fángzi de shuǐguǎn.
examples.english: Workers are replacing the water pipes in the old house.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person crouching low; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
犬 (dog) — a dog crouching beside a person is the old image for lying low.

example.hanzi: 他伏在桌子上睡着了。
example.pinyin: Tā fú zài zhuōzi shang shuìzháo le.
example.english: He fell asleep slumped over the desk.
example.fact: 伏 appears in 起伏 (ups and downs), 伏击 (ambush) and 伏特 (volt). 三伏天, the hottest stretch of summer, is the 'dog days' of the Chinese calendar.

examples.hanzi: 小猫伏在窗台上晒太阳。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎomāo fú zài chuāngtái shàng shài tàiyáng.
examples.english: The kitten is lying on the windowsill sunbathing.

examples.hanzi: 夏天最热的时候叫三伏天。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān zuì rè de shíhou jiào sānfútiān.
examples.english: The hottest period of summer is called the dog days.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — marks bamboo and things woven or made from it, as in 笔 pen, 筷 chopsticks, 箱 box; 篮 is a woven basket.
监 (jiān) is a loose hint for lán; 蓝 lán shares it.

example.hanzi: 她提着一个篮子去买菜。
example.pinyin: Tā tí zhe yí gè lánzi qù mǎicài.
example.english: She carries a basket to buy groceries.
example.fact: 篮 gives 篮子 (basket) and 篮球 (basketball, literally 'basket ball'). 菜篮子 is also a common way to refer to a city's food supply.

examples.hanzi: 学校的篮球场很大。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào de lánqiúchǎng hěn dà.
examples.english: The school's basketball court is large.

examples.hanzi: 她在篮子里放了几个苹果。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài lánzi lǐ fàng le jǐ ge píngguǒ.
examples.english: She put a few apples in the basket.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).

example.hanzi: 他刚说了一半，突然打住不说了。
example.pinyin: Tā gāng shuōle yíbàn, tūrán dǎzhù bù shuō le.
example.english: He had only said half of it when he suddenly stopped talking.
example.fact: The Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962 came to an abrupt halt after thirteen days when Nikita Khrushchev agreed to remove Soviet missiles from Cuba in exchange for a secret US pledge not to invade the island, a resolution reached largely through back-channel letters rather than public negotiation. Declassified records later revealed the crisis came closer to nuclear war than publicly known at the time, when a Soviet submarine captain considered launching a nuclear torpedo before being talked down by a fellow officer. That single decision to stop is often cited as one of the closest calls in modern history.

examples.hanzi: 好了好了，你别再说了，打住吧。
examples.pinyin: Hǎo le hǎo le, nǐ bié zài shuō le, dǎzhù ba.
examples.english: All right, all right, stop talking now.

examples.hanzi: 她的话说到一半被电话打住了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huà shuō dào yībàn bèi diànhuà dǎzhù le.
examples.english: Her speech was cut off halfway by a phone call.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恶 is a bad heart, evil.
亚 (yà) is only a loose sound hint for è.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 警方认定这次纵火事件带有恶意。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng rèndìng zhè cì zònghuǒ shìjiàn dàiyǒu èyì.
example.english: Police determined that the arson incident was carried out with malice.
example.fact: In common law legal systems, 'malice' is a specific technical threshold, not just anger, that separates murder from manslaughter, requiring prosecutors to show intent to kill or a reckless disregard for human life. Malware, the term for malicious software, was coined in 1990 by combining 'malicious' and 'software,' though self-replicating programs go back to the 1971 Creeper worm, created as a harmless experiment on early ARPANET. Cybersecurity researchers now track malware 'families' the way epidemiologists track viruses, tracing shared code back to a common ancestor strain.

examples.hanzi: 网上有人对她发了很多恶意的评论。
examples.pinyin: Wǎngshàng yǒurén duì tā fā le hěn duō èyì de pínglùn.
examples.english: Some people posted many malicious comments about her online.

examples.hanzi: 他并没有恶意，只是开个玩笑。
examples.pinyin: Tā bìng méiyǒu èyì, zhǐshì kāi gè wánxiào.
examples.english: He meant no harm and was just joking.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 腿 leg, 脸 face.
却 (què) is only a loose sound clue for jiǎo.

example.hanzi: 有人在账本上做了手脚。
example.pinyin: Yǒurén zài zhàngběn shàng zuòle shǒujiǎo.
example.english: Someone tampered with the account book.
example.fact: Human hands and feet share the same basic five-digit bone structure, a pattern called pentadactyly that traces back over 350 million years to the first four-limbed vertebrates crawling out of shallow Devonian waters. Feet evolved a rigid arch for weight-bearing walking, while hands kept far more independent finger movement, made possible by an opposable thumb that lets primates grip precisely, a trait shared with few other animals. Forensic accountants use the phrase 'cooking the books' for exactly this kind of hidden manipulation, and modern auditing software now flags suspicious patterns using Benford's Law, the same statistical method that catches irregularities in naturally occurring numbers.

examples.hanzi: 她手脚很麻利，一会儿就做好了饭。
examples.pinyin: Tā shǒujiǎo hěn máli, yīhuǐr jiù zuò hǎo le fàn.
examples.english: She's quick with her hands and feet and cooked the meal in no time.

examples.hanzi: 天太冷了，我的手脚都冻僵了。
examples.pinyin: Tiān tài lěng le, wǒ de shǒujiǎo dōu dòng jiāng le.
examples.english: It's so cold that my hands and feet are frozen stiff.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and links, as in 红, 经, 系: thread gathered into one.
充 (chōng) is only a loose sound clue for tǒng.
一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.

example.hanzi: 秦始皇统一了中国的文字和度量衡。
example.pinyin: Qín Shǐhuáng tǒngyīle Zhōngguó de wénzì hé dùliánghéng.
example.english: Qin Shi Huang unified China's writing system and units of measurement.
example.fact: When Qin Shi Huang unified China's warring states in 221 BC, he also standardized weights, measures, axle widths for carts, and the width of Chinese characters' strokes, changes that made trade and administration across the new empire dramatically more efficient. The same emperor commissioned the terracotta army, over 8,000 life-sized clay soldiers with distinct facial features, buried to guard his tomb. Germany's 1990 reunification is a modern parallel: unifying East and West required reconciling two entirely separate currencies, a process that controversially converted East German marks to West German marks at a 1:1 rate for most personal savings.

examples.hanzi: 大家的意见终于统一了。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā de yìjiàn zhōngyú tǒngyī le.
examples.english: Everyone's opinions have finally been unified.

examples.hanzi: 学校要求学生统一穿校服。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào yāoqiú xuésheng tǒngyī chuān xiàofú.
examples.english: The school requires students to wear a uniform.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to meet is to cross paths.
禺 (yú) is close to yù; same part in 愚 yú and 偶 ǒu.
害 (hài) is a loose sound clue for 割 gē and 辖 xiá; as a word it means to harm, as in 厉害.

example.hanzi: 这位记者在调查腐败案件时不幸遇害。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi jìzhě zài diàochá fǔbài ànjiàn shí bùxìng yùhài.
example.english: This journalist was tragically murdered while investigating a corruption case.
example.fact: The Committee to Protect Journalists has documented well over a thousand journalists killed worldwide since 1992, many while investigating corruption, crime, or conflict, and in a majority of these cases no one is ever convicted. Malta's Daphne Caruana Galizia, killed by a car bomb in 2017 after reporting on government corruption, became a symbol of this impunity, and the investigation into who ordered her death eventually reached senior political figures. International press freedom groups now track an 'impunity index' ranking countries by how rarely journalist killings are ever solved.

examples.hanzi: 据报道，三名游客在山区遇害。
examples.pinyin: Jù bàodào, sān míng yóukè zài shānqū yùhài.
examples.english: According to reports, three tourists were killed in the mountains.

examples.hanzi: 警方正在调查他遇害的原因。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá tā yùhài de yuányīn.
examples.english: The police are investigating why he was murdered.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 板, 样; 模 was a wooden mold or pattern.
莫 (mò) is close to mó; same part in 摸 mō, 膜 mó, 墓 mù.
米 (rice, grain) — marks grain and food, as in 粉, 粮, 糖; 糊 is a paste made from grain.
胡 (hú) gives the sound exactly: 糊 hú, also in 湖 hú and 蝴 hú.

example.hanzi: 照片太模糊，看不清人脸。
example.pinyin: Zhàopiàn tài móhu, kàn bù qīng rénliǎn.
example.english: The photo is too blurry to see the face clearly.
example.fact: Camera blur happens because a lens focuses light from only one distance sharply onto the sensor; anything nearer or farther spreads into a small disc called the circle of confusion. Astronomers faced an extreme version of this problem with the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990 with a mirror ground to the wrong curvature by about 1/50th the width of a human hair, producing blurry images until a 1993 spacewalk installed corrective optics. Modern deconvolution algorithms can now mathematically reverse certain kinds of blur, effectively undoing motion or focus errors after a photo has already been taken.

examples.hanzi: 我对小时候的事只有模糊的记忆。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì xiǎoshíhou de shì zhǐyǒu móhu de jìyì.
examples.english: I only have vague memories of my childhood.

examples.hanzi: 他的回答很模糊，没有说清楚。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huídá hěn móhu, méiyǒu shuō qīngchu.
examples.english: His answer was vague and not clear.

components.note: 水 (water) — a picture of flowing water; as a radical it appears as 氵 on the left (海, 河) or 水 at the bottom (泉, 冰).
日 (sun) — three suns make something brilliantly bright, a crystal; also in 明 bright, 晴 sunny.

example.hanzi: 这个水晶吊灯是从欧洲进口的。
example.pinyin: Zhège shuǐjīng diàodēng shì cóng Ōuzhōu jìnkǒu de.
example.english: This crystal chandelier was imported from Europe.
example.fact: True crystals, whether quartz, diamond, or table salt, are defined by their atoms repeating in a precise, orderly lattice, which is why they naturally form flat faces and sharp geometric edges. Quartz crystals have a useful side effect of this order called the piezoelectric effect, generating a tiny voltage when squeezed, which is exactly what keeps a quartz wristwatch ticking at a steady rate. The largest known natural crystals, giant selenite beams in Mexico's Cave of the Crystals, grew to over 12 meters long over hundreds of thousands of years in a cavern that stayed at a near-perfect, stable 58 degrees Celsius.

examples.hanzi: 她脖子上戴着一条水晶项链。
examples.pinyin: Tā bózi shàng dài zhe yī tiáo shuǐjīng xiàngliàn.
examples.english: She wears a crystal necklace around her neck.

examples.hanzi: 这个水晶球在阳光下闪闪发光。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shuǐjīngqiú zài yángguāng xià shǎnshǎn fāguāng.
examples.english: This crystal ball sparkles in the sunlight.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions of striking or acting: 教, 放, 改, 政; 攻 is to attack.
工 (gōng) sounds exactly like 攻; also in 功 gōng, 红 hóng, 空 kōng.

example.hanzi: 我们的球队正在进攻。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de qiúduì zhèngzài jìngōng.
example.english: Our team is attacking.
example.fact: 攻 has two common uses: attack (进攻, 攻击) and intensive study (攻读 a degree). In modern slang, 攻略 means a walkthrough or travel guide, as in 旅游攻略.

examples.hanzi: 他在大学攻读计算机专业。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué gōngdú jìsuànjī zhuānyè.
examples.english: He studies computer science at university.

examples.hanzi: 对方的进攻很猛，我们要小心防守。
examples.pinyin: Duìfāng de jìngōng hěn měng, wǒmen yào xiǎoxīn fángshǒu.
examples.english: The opponent's attack is fierce, so we need to defend carefully.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 肩 is the shoulder.

example.hanzi: 他的肩膀很宽。
example.pinyin: Tā de jiānbǎng hěn kuān.
example.english: His shoulders are broad.
example.fact: 肩 often takes 膀 in speech (肩膀). It also means 'to bear', as in 肩负 (shoulder a responsibility), and gives 双肩包 (backpack).

examples.hanzi: 我的肩膀有点酸。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiānbǎng yǒudiǎn suān.
examples.english: My shoulders are a bit sore.

examples.hanzi: 她背着一个很重的肩包。
examples.pinyin: Tā bēi zhe yí ge hěn zhòng de jiānbāo.
examples.english: She is carrying a very heavy shoulder bag.

components.note: 夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.
囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.

example.hanzi: 她第一次去外国旅行，感到既紧张又兴奋。
example.pinyin: Tā dì-yī cì qù wàiguó lǚxíng, gǎndào jì jǐnzhāng yòu xīngfèn.
example.english: It was her first trip to a foreign country, and she felt both nervous and excited.
example.fact: The modern passport, as a standardized document required for foreign travel, is a surprisingly recent invention; before World War I, most European travelers crossed borders with no official identification at all. The League of Nations held a conference in 1920 that established the small, booklet-style passport format still used today, largely to manage wartime security concerns that lingered after the conflict ended. Even now, a handful of countries, including North Korea, restrict nearly all outbound foreign travel by their own citizens, making it one of the most controlled borders on Earth.

examples.hanzi: 你有没有去过外国留学？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu méiyǒu qùguo wàiguó liúxué?
examples.english: Have you ever studied abroad?

examples.hanzi: 他的妻子是一个外国人。
examples.pinyin: Tā de qīzi shì yī gè wàiguórén.
examples.english: His wife is a foreigner.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife), as in 到, 别, 利; 剧 first meant to cut deeply, then intense and drama.
居 (jū) — near sound — 剧 is jù; 居 also sounds out 据 jù.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 这座剧场能容纳两千名观众。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò jùchǎng néng róngnà liǎngqiān míng guānzhòng.
example.english: This theater can hold an audience of two thousand people.
example.fact: The Theatre of Epidaurus in ancient Greece, built around 300 BC, seats about 14,000 people and has such precise acoustic design that a coin dropped on the central stage can reportedly be heard clearly from the topmost row, a feat researchers attribute partly to the limestone seating scattering low-frequency crowd noise while preserving higher-pitched speech. London's Globe Theatre, where many of Shakespeare's plays premiered, burned down in 1613 after a cannon effect during a performance of Henry VIII set the thatched roof alight. Modern theater design still borrows the ancient Greek amphitheater's fan-shaped seating because it gives the largest number of seats a clear line of sight to the stage.

examples.hanzi: 我们明晚在市中心的剧场看戏。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngwǎn zài shì zhōngxīn de jùchǎng kàn xì.
examples.english: Tomorrow night we're watching a play at the downtown theater.

examples.hanzi: 剧场的灯光暗下来，演出开始了。
examples.pinyin: Jùchǎng de dēngguāng àn xiàlái, yǎnchū kāishǐ le.
examples.english: The theater lights dimmed and the show began.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.
向 (toward) — a window 口 in a wall facing a direction, hence toward. It also gives its sound to 响 xiǎng and 饷 xiǎng.

example.hanzi: 所有的证据都指向同一个结论。
example.pinyin: Suǒyǒu de zhèngjù dōu zhǐxiàng tóng yí gè jiélùn.
example.english: All the evidence points towards the same conclusion.
example.fact: A compass needle points toward magnetic north, not true geographic north, because Earth's magnetic poles drift over time and currently sit hundreds of kilometers from the rotational poles; the magnetic north pole has been moving toward Siberia at an accelerating pace in recent decades. Sailors have long corrected for this gap, called magnetic declination, using charts that show exactly how many degrees a compass reading differs from true north at a given location. Some animals, including migratory birds and sea turtles, appear to sense this same magnetic field directly, using it as an internal compass to navigate thousands of kilometers without any visible landmarks.

examples.hanzi: 时钟的指针指向了十二点。
examples.pinyin: Shízhōng de zhǐzhēn zhǐxiàng le shí'èr diǎn.
examples.english: The clock hands pointed to twelve.

examples.hanzi: 调查结果指向了一个意外的结论。
examples.pinyin: Diàochá jiéguǒ zhǐxiàng le yī gè yìwài de jiélùn.
examples.english: The investigation results pointed to an unexpected conclusion.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — a hand, as in 对, 寻, 守; with 圭 (a heap of earth) it means heaping earth to mark a border, then to seal.
门 (gate, door) — 门 is a gate, as in 开, 关, 问, 间; 闭 puts a bar across it, so shut.

example.hanzi: 由于施工，这条路暂时封闭了。
example.pinyin: Yóuyú shīgōng, zhè tiáo lù zànshí fēngbì le.
example.english: Due to construction, this road is temporarily closed off.
example.fact: North Korea's border and information environment is often cited as the most closed off in the modern world, with the state controlling nearly all internet access and a domestic intranet called Kwangmyong standing in for the global web most citizens will never see. Historically, medieval Venice sealed off entire neighborhoods during plague outbreaks, and the 40-day isolation period it imposed on ships, called 'quarantena' in Venetian dialect, is the direct origin of the modern word 'quarantine.' Sealed environments are also deliberately built for science: Biosphere 2 in Arizona closed eight people inside an airtight glass structure for two years in the early 1990s to test whether humans could survive in a fully self-contained ecosystem.

examples.hanzi: 这个小区实行封闭式管理。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎoqū shíxíng fēngbìshì guǎnlǐ.
examples.english: This residential complex has gated management.

examples.hanzi: 房间太封闭了，空气不流通。
examples.pinyin: Fángjiān tài fēngbì le, kōngqì bù liútōng.
examples.english: The room is too closed in, and the air doesn't circulate.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
册 — bamboo slips bound with a cord, the ancient book; today a volume or register, as in 手册 manual, 注册 register.

example.hanzi: 新员工入职时会拿到一本员工手册。
example.pinyin: Xīn yuángōng rùzhí shí huì nádào yì běn yuángōng shǒucè.
example.english: New employees receive an employee handbook when they join.
example.fact: NASA's Apollo astronauts carried checklists and reference cards, essentially condensed manuals, sewn directly onto the fabric of their spacesuit sleeves, since there was no time in an emergency to flip through a bound book. The Chicago Manual of Style, first published in 1906, has gone through 17 editions and remains one of the most widely used style manuals in American publishing, now running to over a thousand pages. IKEA's famously wordless assembly manuals, using only illustrations, were a deliberate design choice starting in the 1950s so a single instruction sheet could work in every country the furniture was sold, without any translation at all.

examples.hanzi: 请先阅读产品手册再使用。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiān yuèdú chǎnpǐn shǒucè zài shǐyòng.
examples.english: Please read the product manual before using it.

examples.hanzi: 旅游手册上有很多实用的信息。
examples.pinyin: Lǚyóu shǒucè shàng yǒu hěn duō shíyòng de xìnxī.
examples.english: The travel handbook has lots of practical information.

components.note: 首 (head, first) — a picture of a head with hair on top, which became the word for first and chief: 首先, 元首, also a measure for songs.
要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.

example.hanzi: 安全是这次任务的首要考虑。
example.pinyin: Ānquán shì zhè cì rènwù de shǒuyào kǎolǜ.
example.english: Safety is the primary consideration for this mission.
example.fact: Maslow's 1943 hierarchy of needs argued that basic physiological needs, like food, water, and sleep, must be satisfied before a person can meaningfully prioritize anything higher, such as safety, belonging, or self-actualization. In aviation, pilots are trained around the mnemonic 'aviate, navigate, communicate,' a strict priority order that puts simply keeping the aircraft flying above every other task, even an emergency radio call. NASA engineers designing the Apollo Guidance Computer built in a similar priority system, letting it drop lower-priority tasks automatically during the tense final descent of Apollo 11 when it became briefly overloaded with alarms.

examples.hanzi: 对学生来说，学习是首要任务。
examples.pinyin: Duì xuésheng lái shuō, xuéxí shì shǒuyào rènwu.
examples.english: For students, studying is the top priority.

examples.hanzi: 医生说，首要的事情是让病人休息。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō, shǒuyào de shìqing shì ràng bìngrén xiūxi.
examples.english: The doctor said the most important thing is to let the patient rest.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — the frame on the left and top, as in 原, 厚, 压. In 厌 it is just the old cliff-like frame of 厭.
犬 (quǎn, dog) — looks like a sound part but quǎn vs yàn is only a loose hint. The old 厭 got its sound from 猒 (yàn).
火 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 灯 lamp, 烧 burn, 热 hot: a hot, fevered head, hence vexed.
页 (head) is a loose sound clue for fán; as a meaning part 页 means head or page.

example.hanzi: 他对这份重复性的工作感到厌烦。
example.pinyin: Tā duì zhè fèn chóngfùxìng de gōngzuò gǎndào yànfán.
example.english: He feels fed up with this repetitive job.
example.fact: Psychologists studying boredom classify it as a distinct emotional state, not merely an absence of stimulation, and have found it reliably activates brain regions associated with the desire to escape one's current situation. A 2014 study published in Science found that many people would rather give themselves a mild electric shock than sit alone with their thoughts for just 15 minutes, showing how aversive plain boredom can feel. Long-duration studies of astronauts and Antarctic research station workers show that monotony, not danger, is often the psychological factor crews report struggling with most over months of isolation.

examples.hanzi: 我对每天挤地铁感到厌烦。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì měitiān jǐ dìtiě gǎndào yànfán.
examples.english: I'm fed up with squeezing onto the subway every day.

examples.hanzi: 孩子的哭闹让他感到很厌烦。
examples.pinyin: Háizi de kūnào ràng tā gǎndào hěn yànfán.
examples.english: The child's crying made him feel very annoyed.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — marks garments and cloth, as in 衫 shirt, 裤 trousers, 裙 skirt; 衬 is the lining or shirt worn close to the body.
寸 (cùn) is only a loose sound hint for chèn.
衣 (clothes) — a picture of a coat with a collar and sleeves. As a radical it is 衤 on the left: 裤 trousers, 衬 shirt, 被 quilt.

example.hanzi: 他今天穿了一件白色的衬衣。
example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān chuānle yí jiàn báisè de chènyī.
example.english: He is wearing a white shirt today.
example.fact: The button-down collar shirt was invented in 1900 after American businessman John Brooks watched English polo players button their collars down to keep them from flapping in the wind, and brought the idea back to found what became Brooks Brothers' signature style. Cotton, the fiber behind most shirts, only became cheap and widespread after Eli Whitney's 1793 cotton gin mechanized the labor-intensive process of separating seeds from fiber, a shift that also dramatically expanded plantation slavery in the American South. Today, a single cotton shirt can require over 2,000 liters of water to produce, once irrigation for the raw cotton is counted.

examples.hanzi: 这件衬衣太小了，我想换大一号的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn chènyī tài xiǎo le, wǒ xiǎng huàn dà yī hào de.
examples.english: This shirt is too small, so I want to swap it for a larger size.

examples.hanzi: 他把衬衣塞进裤子里，显得很整齐。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ chènyī sāi jìn kùzi lǐ, xiǎnde hěn zhěngqí.
examples.english: He tucked his shirt into his trousers and looked neat.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 这座豪宅雇了一位管家来打理日常事务。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò háozhái gùle yí wèi guǎnjiā lái dǎlǐ rìcháng shìwù.
example.english: This mansion hired a butler to manage day-to-day affairs.
example.fact: The word 'butler' comes from the Old French 'bouteillier,' meaning the servant in charge of the wine bottles, reflecting the role's original, narrower duty of managing a household's cellar before it expanded to overseeing entire estates. Britain's Ivor Spencer founded a formal butler training school in 1981 that still certifies graduates for households and royal families around the world, teaching everything from table etiquette to discreet security awareness. Modern 'smart home' systems are sometimes marketed as digital butlers, though surveys of professional butlers note that judgment, discretion, and reading a household's unspoken needs remain far harder to automate than simply turning on lights.

examples.hanzi: 这位管家把家里的事安排得井井有条。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi guǎnjiā bǎ jiālǐ de shì ānpái de jǐngjǐngyǒutiáo.
examples.english: The steward arranged household affairs in perfect order.

examples.hanzi: 小说里的管家其实是个秘密侦探。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoshuō lǐ de guǎnjiā qíshí shì gè mìmì zhēntàn.
examples.english: The butler in the novel is actually a secret detective.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body parts, as in 脸 face, 肝 liver; 脉 is the network of vessels branching through the body.
扌 (hand) — striking and grappling; also in 打 hit, 抱 hold.
尃 (fū) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 博 bó, 簿 bù and 薄 báo.

example.hanzi: 医生正在检查病人的脉搏。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng zhèngzài jiǎnchá bìngrén de màibó.
example.english: The doctor is checking the patient's pulse.
example.fact: A resting adult human pulse typically ranges from 60 to 100 beats per minute, but elite endurance athletes can have resting rates as low as 30 to 40 because years of training enlarge the heart's chambers, letting each beat pump more blood. Traditional Chinese medicine practitioners have long used detailed pulse-taking at the wrist, distinguishing dozens of named pulse qualities, as a core diagnostic method dating back over two thousand years. Blue whales, the largest animals ever known, have hearts so massive that their resting heart rate can drop to just two beats per minute while diving, the slowest heartbeat ever recorded in an animal.

examples.hanzi: 护士用手指按着他的脉搏数了一分钟。
examples.pinyin: Hùshi yòng shǒuzhǐ àn zhe tā de màibó shǔ le yī fēnzhōng.
examples.english: The nurse pressed his pulse with her fingers and counted for one minute.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市的脉搏随着夜晚的到来而加快。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì de màibó suízhe yèwǎn de dàolái ér jiākuài.
examples.english: The city's pulse quickens as night arrives.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks soil and dust, as in 地, 城, 墙; 埃 is fine dust.
矣 (yǐ) is a loose hint for āi; 唉 āi and 挨 āi share the part.
文 (writing, culture) — a person with a patterned chest, early tattooed designs, which became writing and culture. Also in 纹 wén and 蚊 wén.

example.hanzi: 我的朋友埃文来自加拿大。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyou Āiwén láizì Jiānádà.
example.english: My friend Evan is from Canada.
example.fact: The name Evan is a Welsh form of John, ultimately derived from the Hebrew name Yochanan meaning 'God is gracious,' and it entered wider English use partly through Welsh migration into England during the medieval and early modern periods. Evan Williams, a co-founder of both Blogger and Twitter, helped shape two of the internet's most influential publishing platforms of the early 2000s and 2010s. Naming trends researchers have tracked 'Evan' as one of many biblical-root names that surged in English-speaking countries during the late 20th century, following a broader pattern of parents favoring softer, single-syllable-sounding names.

examples.hanzi: 埃文住在我们隔壁，常常来借工具。
examples.pinyin: Āiwén zhù zài wǒmen gébì, chángcháng lái jiè gōngjù.
examples.english: Evan lives next door and often comes to borrow tools.

examples.hanzi: 你认识那个叫埃文的新同事吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi nàge jiào Āiwén de xīn tóngshì ma?
examples.english: Do you know the new colleague named Evan?

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 叮 is a sound, a sting or a reminder, as in 叮嘱 urge.
丁 (dīng) — same sound: 叮 dīng. 丁 also sounds out 钉 dīng and 盯 dīng.

example.hanzi: 我被蚊子叮了一下。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bèi wénzi dīng le yíxià.
example.english: I was bitten by a mosquito.
example.fact: 叮 covers insect bites (被蚊子叮) and pressing someone (叮嘱, 'to instruct repeatedly'). 叮咚 is the sound of a bell or drops of water.

examples.hanzi: 他的手臂上被叮了好几个包。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shǒubì shàng bèi dīng le hǎojǐ ge bāo.
examples.english: His arm got several bites from insects.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈叮嘱我路上要小心。
examples.pinyin: Māma dīngzhǔ wǒ lùshàng yào xiǎoxīn.
examples.english: Mom reminded me to be careful on the road.

components.note: 己 (oneself) — dictionary reads it as a loom with thread; scholars are not sure. Memory aid: a curled-up figure turned in on itself — 'self'. Sound clue in 记 纪 (jì) and 起 (qǐ).

example.hanzi: 你要相信自己。
example.pinyin: Nǐ yào xiāngxìn zìjǐ.
example.english: You should believe in yourself.
example.fact: 己 almost always appears in 自己 (oneself), 知己 (a soulmate) and the Confucian line 己所不欲，勿施于人. Don't confuse it with 已 (yǐ) and 巳 (sì): 己 is open at the top, 已 half closed, 巳 fully closed.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该先管好自己。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi xiān guǎn hǎo zìjǐ.
examples.english: We should first manage ourselves well.

examples.hanzi: 不要总是想着利己的事。
examples.pinyin: Bú yào zǒngshì xiǎng zhe lìjǐ de shì.
examples.english: Do not always think about things that only benefit yourself.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — marks cloth, as in 衬, 衫, 裤; 补 is to mend a garment.
卜 (bǔ) gives the sound exactly: 补 bǔ.
亠 (lid) — the top part, a cap. Memory aid: a lid on top of 允 suggests something filled up to the lid, hence 'fill, be full' as in 充满.
允 (yǔn, permit) — the bottom part; it is a visible piece, but not a sound clue today (充 is chōng). Memory aid: allowed to fill up.

example.hanzi: 医生建议他每天补充维生素D。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì tā měitiān bǔchōng wéishēngsù D.
example.english: The doctor recommended he supplement his vitamin D daily.
example.fact: Vitamin D is unusual among vitamins because the human body can manufacture it itself, synthesizing it in the skin through a chemical reaction triggered by ultraviolet B sunlight, which is why deficiency is more common in winter or at high latitudes. Sailors' historical struggle with a different deficiency, scurvy from lack of vitamin C, was solved centuries before anyone understood vitamins existed; James Lind's 1747 citrus experiment is considered one of the first controlled clinical trials in medical history. The global dietary supplement industry is now estimated to be worth well over 150 billion dollars a year, despite mixed scientific evidence on the benefit of many products for people who are not actually deficient.

examples.hanzi: 如果有什么要补充的，请现在说。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ yǒu shénme yào bǔchōng de, qǐng xiànzài shuō.
examples.english: If you have anything to add, please say it now.

examples.hanzi: 运动后要及时补充水分。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòng hòu yào jíshí bǔchōng shuǐfèn.
examples.english: After exercise, you should replenish fluids promptly.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.
禾 (grain) — crops: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 私 was grain held for oneself.
厶 (sī) is the ancient form of 私 itself, meaning private; 公 gōng (public) is its opposite.

example.hanzi: 海关查获了一批走私的象牙。
example.pinyin: Hǎiguān cháhuòle yì pī zǒusī de xiàngyá.
example.english: Customs seized a batch of smuggled ivory.
example.fact: During the era of British trade in China, the East India Company effectively ran state-sponsored opium smuggling into the country on a massive scale, a trade that triggered the First Opium War in 1839 after Chinese authorities tried to seize and destroy smuggled stockpiles. Modern wildlife smuggling, including ivory, rhino horn, and pangolin scales, is now estimated by INTERPOL to be worth up to 20 billion dollars a year, ranking among the largest illegal trades after drugs and counterfeit goods. Customs agencies increasingly use CT scanners originally developed for medical imaging to spot smuggled goods hidden inside sealed cargo containers without ever opening them.

examples.hanzi: 他因为走私香烟被警察抓住了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi zǒusī xiāngyān bèi jǐngchá zhuā zhù le.
examples.english: He was caught by the police for smuggling cigarettes.

examples.hanzi: 这个走私团伙活动了很多年。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zǒusī tuánhuǒ huódòng le hěn duō nián.
examples.english: This smuggling ring has been active for many years.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: fear is a feeling.
白 (bái) is a close sound clue for pà; 白 also in 拍 pāi and 伯 bó.

example.hanzi: 消防员不怕危险，冲进火场救人。
example.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán bùpà wēixiǎn, chōngjìn huǒchǎng jiùrén.
example.english: The firefighters, unafraid of danger, rushed into the fire to save people.
example.fact: A small number of people worldwide have a rare genetic condition called Urbach-Wiethe disease, which damages the amygdala and leaves them almost entirely unable to feel ordinary fear, a case famously studied in a patient known in research literature as 'SM,' who showed no fear even when confronted with snakes, spiders, or horror films. Firefighters, by contrast, train specifically to manage fear rather than eliminate it, since researchers have found that some baseline fear response actually improves decision-making and risk assessment under pressure. Free solo climber Alex Honnold, who scales cliffs without ropes, was found in a 2016 brain scan study to have an amygdala that required unusually strong stimulation before showing any fear response at all.

examples.hanzi: 只要你不怕苦，就一定能成功。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyào nǐ bù pà kǔ, jiù yīdìng néng chénggōng.
examples.english: As long as you aren't afraid of hardship, you will surely succeed.

examples.hanzi: 他不怕黑，一个人也敢走夜路。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù pà hēi, yī gè rén yě gǎn zǒu yèlù.
examples.english: He is not afraid of the dark and dares to walk alone at night.

components.note: 歹 (bad bone) — death and decay, as in 残 remnant, 烈 fierce, 殊 special.
匕 (person) — a person beside bones: death.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这场战争造成了大量死人。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng zhànzhēng zàochéngle dàliàng sǐrén.
example.english: This war caused a huge number of deaths.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptian mummification, developed over roughly 3,000 years, involved removing internal organs (except the heart, believed to hold a person's intelligence), packing the body with a salt-like substance called natron, and wrapping it in hundreds of meters of linen, all aimed at preserving the body for the afterlife. Forensic scientists studying decomposition run outdoor 'body farms,' most famously at the University of Tennessee since 1981, where donated cadavers decompose under controlled, monitored conditions to help police estimate time of death in real investigations. Bog bodies, corpses preserved for millennia in low-oxygen, acidic peat bogs across Northern Europe, can retain skin, hair, and even stomach contents intact enough for scientists to reconstruct a person's last meal thousands of years later.

examples.hanzi: 这条路上经常出车祸死人，大家都很担心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù shàng jīngcháng chū chēhuò sǐ rén, dàjiā dōu hěn dānxīn.
examples.english: Fatal car accidents often happen on this road, and everyone is worried.

examples.hanzi: 别装死人了，快起来吃饭！
examples.pinyin: Bié zhuāng sǐrén le, kuài qǐlái chīfàn!
examples.english: Stop playing dead and get up to eat!
